L16: > Abstract:Real-valued differential forms on Berkovich analytic spaces were introduced by Chambert-Loir and Ducros in 'Formes différentielles réelles et courants sur les espaces de Berkovich' using superforms on polyhedral complexes. We prove a Poincaré lemma for these superforms and use it to also prove a Poincaré lemma for real-valued differential forms on Berkovich spaces.
L17: For superforms we further show finite dimensionality for the associated de Rham cohomology on polyhedral complexes in all (bi-)degrees. We also show finite dimensionality for the real-valued de Rham cohomology of the analytification of an algebraic variety in some bidegrees.

L32@P0: 1. Introduction
L33@P0: Chambert-Loir and Ducros recently introduced smooth real-valued differential forms on Berkovich analytic spaces [CLD12]. Basic ingredients in this
L34@P0: new theory are Lagerberg’s superforms [Lag12] and new methods from tropical geometry (see for example [Gub12]). Chambert-Loir and Ducros also
L35@P0: introduce currents, develop basic results of pluripotential theory (in particular an analogue of Bedford-Taylor theory), show a Poincaré-Lelong formula
L36@P0: and construct Monge-Ampère measures on Berkovich analytic spaces. There
L37@P0: has also been recent work by Gubler and Künnemann [GK14] where they
L38@P0-1: 12 PHILIPP JELL
L39@P1: extend the results by Chambert-Loir and Ducros and give a Berkovich analytic construction of local heights. The results mentioned above show that
L40@P1: the forms introduced by Chambert-Loir and Ducros are of basic interest and
L41@P1: should play for example a crucial role in (non-Archimedean) Arakelov theory.
L42@P1: It is the aim of this paper to prove some foundational results about the differential forms of Chambert-Loir and Ducros. More precisely we will show
L43@P1: that they satisfy a Poincaré lemma and we will investigate their de Rham
L44@P1: cohomology.
L45@P1: Our main object of study is the space of real-valued differential forms introduced by Chambert-Loir and Ducros, which are bigraded and have differential operators d, d
L46@P1: ′ and d′′ analogous to the operators d, ∂ and ∂ for
L47@P1: differential forms on complex manifolds. We are interested in the de Rham
L48@P1: cohomology defined by these operators. Since these forms are locally defined
L49@P1: by superforms on polyhedral complexes, we will prove a Poincaré lemma for
L50@P1: superforms on polyhedral complexes. From this we can deduce finiteness of
L51@P1: the de Rham cohomology of superforms on polyhedral complexes, using techniques analogous to those from differential geometry. We will also deduce
L52@P1: a Poincaré lemma for forms on Berkovich spaces. With the help of sheaf
L53@P1: theory we can then deduce that in some bidegrees this cohomology depends
L54@P1: only on the underlying topological space of the Berkovich space and agrees
L55@P1: with singular cohomology. Finally the theory of skeletons enables us to show
L56@P1: that in these degrees cohomology is finite dimensional in many cases.
L57@P1: In section 2 we recall the construction of superforms on polyhedral complexes
L58@P1: (as introduced by Lagerberg in [Lag12], see as well [CLD12] and [Gub13])
L59@P1: and prove a Poincaré lemma for these forms (Theorem 2.16). The usual
L60@P1: pullback of differential forms applied to superforms commutes with the differential operator along affine maps. For arbitrary maps this is false (cf.
L61@P1: 2.7). Our proof of the Poincaré lemma follows the proof in the classical
L62@P1: case. A crucial new tool is the introduction of a pullback of superforms
L63@P1: via C∞-maps, which commutes with the differential operator. We use this
L64@P1: to prove a homotopy formula in Theorem 2.12. This will be the key result
L65@P1: to prove the d
L66@P1: ′
L67@P1: -Poincaré lemma. In section 3 we prove finiteness of the de
L68@P1: Rham cohomology defined by superforms, using good covers and the MayerVietoris sequence. In section 4 we introduce real-valued differential forms
L69@P1: on analytifications of algebraic varieties following Gubler’s presentation in
L70@P1: [Gub13]. Then we use our result for polyhedral complexes to prove the
L71@P1: Poincaré lemma for real-valued differential forms on the analytification of
L72@P1: an algebraic variety (Theorem 4.5). Afterwards we sketch the argument for
L73@P1: a generalization to a paracompact good analytic space (Theorem 4.8). In
L74@P1: Theorem 4.9 we show that, as a consequence, for a variety X the cohomology
L75@P1: of the complex (A•,0(Xan), d′) is finite dimensional.
